title: QA plan file
description: Reviewable intermediate artifact produced by the qa-xray agent and consumed by .claude/scripts/xray-push.mjs.

project.description: Jira project key the Tests are created in, e.g. "EC".

source.description: The ticket these tests were derived from.

summary.description: The ticket's summary when the plan was written. spec-drift.mjs compares it against the live one to catch a repurposed ticket.

acDigest.description: Digest of the ticket's acceptance-criteria section when the plan was written, written by spec-drift.mjs --record. Catches the common case a summary comparison cannot: same title, rewritten criteria.

acCheckedOn.description: ISO date the digest was recorded, so an unreviewed plan is visible as such.

folder.description: Default Xray Test Repository folder path, e.g. "/Header/Megamenu".

previewBase.description: Origin the fixture paths are opened from, e.g. https://develop--ufs--foodsolutions-04.aem.page. Branch-specific by nature, so it is stated once here rather than baked into a step — the Test Execution's environment records which branch a result belongs to.

testSets.description: Optional override of the Test Set summary per suite. Omit it — the default is three project-wide sets ("Sanity testing", "Regression testing", "E2E testing") that accumulate tests across every ticket. Naming them here creates ticket-scoped sets instead, since the registry is keyed by summary.

fixtures.description: Authored test content in Document Authoring, generated rather than hand-built. A step cites a fixture instead of describing the authoring work, which is what makes a small number of broad tests workable.

id.description: Stable identity, e.g. BRANDS-FX-01. Never renumber one — tests cite it.

purpose.description: What this fixture exists to prove, in one line.

page.description: Path of the fixture page in DA, e.g. /drafts/qa/brands/happy. Never under a published path.

nav.description: A nav document generated for this fixture by transforming a live one. Header-family blocks live in the site-wide nav, so a variant means a whole nav rather than a section; the page's `nav` metadata row is derived from `path` automatically. A spec may edit more than one region: `utility` for the top bar, `logo` and `menus` for the nav row itself, and the count/label/links keys for the brand strip inside the Products megamenu.

path.description: Where the generated nav is written, under /drafts/.

from.description: The live document it is derived from, e.g. /nav. Deriving keeps the fixture identical to production except on the axis under test.

count.description: How many brand links the strip should hold. Logos cycle from the source when more are wanted than exist.

label.description: Replacement text for the strip label.

removeLabel.description: Drop the label entirely, for the degraded case.

links.description: Per-link overrides, positional: { alt, src, caption }.

utility.description: Edits to the nav's utility bar — its first section, holding the author-defined links and the language block.

links.description: Utility links as "Label|/href", replacing the authored list.

trigger.description: The language switcher's trigger label, e.g. ":globe: United States · EN".

languages.description: Language options as "Label · CODE|/href". One entry is the single-language market case.

note.description: The country note shown under the language list.

logo.description: Edits to the nav's logo. The Content Slots table gives it one fallback — text brand when there is no image — and an author produces that by typing the brand name where the icon token was.

text.description: Replaces the logo icon with this text, keeping the link around it.

menus.description: Edits to the nav's top-level items. Each item is one div.nav-menu block: row 1 is the link shown on the bar, rows 2+ are its megamenu columns. Items are built by cycling the live blocks, so a fixture with six items still carries real megamenu content.

items.description: The top-level items, in bar order.

label.description: The label shown on the bar.

plain.description: Drop the megamenu columns, leaving a link with nothing to open. That absence is what makes an item plain — there is no flag in the content model.

promo.description: Edits to a megamenu's promotional tile. The tile has no block and no class of its own: it is a submenu row whose first cell holds loose paragraphs — eyebrow, **title**, an optional description, then the CTA — and the implementation reads meaning out of that order. Which variant it becomes is decided by POSITION, not by the author: the panel's first child is the light `.nav-feature`, any later child the dark `.nav-promo`. One entry per tile edited.

menu.description: Which megamenu to edit, named as it reads on the bar (e.g. "Products"). Omit to take the first menu that already has a tile.

target.description: Which existing tile to edit when a panel holds both — Recipes ships a leading feature and a trailing promo. Defaults to the first.

position.description: Where the tile is authored among the panel's rows, and so which variant it becomes: "first" is the light feature, "last" a dark promo after the columns. Omit to edit the tile where it already sits, so a copy change does not silently change the variant too.

remove.description: Drop the tile entirely, for the panel-with-no-promo case.

eyebrow.description: The overline label, authored as the first paragraph.

title.description: The title, authored bold — which is how the implementation finds it.

strongTitle.description: Set false for the author who forgot the bold. The classifier then falls back to the second paragraph.

description.description: The body paragraph. The content model gives it to the feature only; authoring one on a promo is a real case and lands on .nav-promo-desc, which has no styling of its own.

extraCta.description: A second CTA, as "Label|/href". The content model forbids it and nothing enforces that, so a fixture can prove what happens.

ctaIcon.description: Author a trailing :arrow: icon token on the CTA. The stylesheet sizes an authored icon; it no longer draws an arrow of its own.

ctaInSecondCell.description: Author the CTA in the row's second cell. Links there with no bold title reclassify the whole row as a labelled column — the mis-authoring that costs the tile its card.

sections.description: Sections on the page, in order. Omit for a fixture whose content is entirely in its nav document.

id.description: Stable identity, and the idempotency key for pushes — NEVER renumber one. Prefer a feature slug (BRANDS-TC-01) over a ticket key (EC-14-TC-01): spec tickets get repurposed and renumbered, features do not.

summary.description: Jira summary. The format is defined once, in the Conventions section of .claude/agents/qa-xray.md — do not restate it here, because two statements of it drift apart.

ac.description: Acceptance criteria this test traces to. May be empty ONLY for a standing requirement the agent must cover whether or not the ticket mentions it (WCAG 2.1 AA, RTL) — and such a test must then explain itself in `notes` and be listed under Coverage gaps. xray-push enforces that pairing; an empty list with no explanation is rejected.

labels.description: Extra dimension labels; whitespace is hyphenated on push.

scope.description: What this test covers, in plain English, for a reader who has not read the ticket. Published into the Jira description.

fixtures.description: Fixture ids this test runs against. Their URLs are published into the Jira description so a tester never has to author anything.

precondition.description: Environment state required before step 1, beyond opening a fixture.

projectId.description: Numeric Jira project id, required only to pre-create the Test Repository folder (EC = 11590).

assignee.description: Atlassian accountId to assign every created Test to. Omit to leave unassigned.

feature.description: Feature slug these tests belong to; matches the prefix of every test id.
